statement: Account A has $1{,}000$ dollars, and $50$ dollars is added to it at the end of each year. Account B has $800$ dollars and earns $8\%$ interest, compounded at the end of each year. No other money is added or removed. After how many years will the balance in account B first be greater than the balance in account A?

choices.misconception: I treated account A as staying at $1{,}000$ dollars, and $800(1.08)^3 \approx 1{,}008$ is the first balance of B above $1{,}000$.
I found the last year in which account B is still behind account A and gave that year.
I treated account B as growing by $8\%$ of $800$, or $64$ dollars, every year, so I solved $800 + 64t > 1{,}000 + 50t$.

hints: After $t$ years, A has $1{,}000 + 50t$ dollars and B has $800(1.08)^t$ dollars.
Make a table of both balances, year by year, starting around $t = 5$.
At $t = 6$: A has $1{,}300$ and B has about $1{,}269.50$. At $t = 7$: A has $1{,}350$ and B has about $1{,}371.06$.

solutions.reliable: After $t$ years the balances are $A = 1{,}000 + 50t$ and $B = 800(1.08)^t$. At $t = 5$: $A = 1{,}250$ and $B \approx 1{,}175.46$. At $t = 6$: $A = 1{,}300$ and $B \approx 1{,}269.50$. At $t = 7$: $A = 1{,}350$ and $B \approx 1{,}371.06$. Before $t = 7$ account B is behind, and at $t = 7$ it is ahead for the first time, so the answer is $7$ years.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
